title: React Basics: Building Reusable Components with Vite
summary: Set up a React project with Vite, clean up the starter template, and build reusable Header, Footer, and Food components using JSX and embedded JavaScript expressions.

steps.title: Scaffold and run Vite React app
steps.instructions: Open a project folder in VS Code, launch the integrated terminal, and run npm create vite@latest choosing my-react-app, React, and JavaScript. Change into my-react-app, run npm install, and start the dev server with npm run dev.
steps.expected_output: VITE v4.4.9  ready in 221 ms Local: http://localhost:5173/

targets.caption: Start the Vite development server inside my-react-app

hints: Make sure you opened the integrated terminal inside your project folder before scaffolding.
After npm create vite@latest finishes, run cd my-react-app before running npm install.
Run npm run dev and open the printed http://localhost:5173/ URL in your browser.
common_mistakes: Running npm install or npm run dev in the parent folder instead of cd my-react-app.
Selecting TypeScript instead of JavaScript when prompted for a variant.

steps.title: Clean up sample App component
steps.instructions: Delete the sample code inside function App() and remove the unused imports at the top of src/App.jsx. Delete src/App.css from the Explorer sidebar.

targets.caption: Keep only the empty App function and default export

explanations.topic: Role of App.jsx as the root component

hints: Remove the entire body of function App() so the starter counter disappears.
Delete the four import lines at the top of src/App.jsx as well.
Leave export default App at the bottom and delete src/App.css.
common_mistakes: Accidentally deleting export default App, which breaks the import in main.jsx.
Leaving unused imports for App.css after deleting the stylesheet file.

targets.caption: Import and render the Header component inside App

explanations.topic: Returning a single root element from a component

hints: Component file and function names should start with an uppercase letter: Header.jsx and function Header().
Make sure src/Header.jsx ends with export default Header and is saved.
In src/App.jsx, add import Header from './Header.jsx' and return <Header/> inside App().
common_mistakes: Using lowercase <header/> instead of <Header/> in App.jsx, which renders an HTML header tag instead of your component.
Forgetting to save Header.jsx before checking the browser.

steps.title: Render Footer inside a fragment
steps.instructions: Import Footer in src/App.jsx and place <Footer/> below <Header/>. Wrap both components in a React fragment <>...</> so App returns a single enclosing tag.

targets.caption: Wrap sibling components in an empty JSX fragment

explanations.topic: Fixing adjacent JSX elements error with fragments

hints: Returning <Header/> and <Footer/> side by side without a parent causes a Babel syntax error.
Enclose both <Header/> and <Footer/> inside an empty tag pair <> and </>.
Check that import Footer from './Footer.jsx' is present at the top of App.jsx.
common_mistakes: Returning adjacent JSX elements (<Header/> and <Footer/>) without wrapping them in <>...</>.
Typing an extra opening <> instead of closing with </>.

targets.caption: Embed JavaScript inside JSX using curly braces

explanations.topic: Inserting JavaScript inside JSX return with curly braces

hints: Use curly braces {} inside JSX whenever you want to evaluate JavaScript.
Call new Date().getFullYear() inside the curly braces.

Your paragraph line should read:

common_mistakes: Omitting curly braces so new Date().getFullYear() renders as literal text.
Omitting parentheses on Date() or getFullYear().
